results.name: fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome
results.problems:
No strays: git status --porcelain before staging showed only src/combat.c, src/combat.h, tests/combat.c and tools/code_emit/data/emit_state.json, all inside the pipeline's own paths, so no separate stray commit was needed and none was made.

Ghidra: the emit verdict's ghidra_fixes was empty; the review verdict carried one "plate" fix at 00019f80, applied as an append to the existing Rebuild note (fetched the current plate first and re-set it whole, so the note reads as one paragraph and nothing else in the plate moved). Baseline audit after the change: orphan code ranges 0, error bookmarks 0, undefined bytes in .object1 0. Program saved, snapshot re-exported (the one-line diff in ghidra_snapshot/comments.txt is that plate).

Encoding verification note: printing the appended text to the console did render the Traditional Chinese as mojibake, but that is the console pipe, not the file. Verified numerically instead -- the four appended strings are string-equal to the ones parsed out of the verdict files, the CJK run in the second entry has codepoints 0x5c1a 0x672a 0x89e3 0x8b80 (尚未解讀), and the whole emit_issues.json contains zero U+FFFD. The file diff is 14 insertions and 0 deletions, so the 35 pre-existing address keys round-tripped byte-identically. Both appended entries carry "status": "open" and "from": "emit" (the review verdict's open_issues was empty).

emit_state.json: the 00019f80 entry only -- status in_flight -> committed, emitted_against "0x3e2" added, in_flight_since dropped, rounds 0 -> 1 as instructed. Diff is a pure 8-line addition at that key, no other entry touched.

Commit message was written to a UTF-8 file and committed with git commit -F --cleanup=verbatim rather than passed through the shell; verified afterwards by comparing the raw commit object's bytes to the expected UTF-8 (exact match, no BOM), and git log --oneline --grep "@ 00019f80" returns exactly one hit.
